correctness.rationale: For every nonisolated x the localized cost of moving mass into or out of x is at least r a_x>0; the normalized transport estimate controls |mu(x)-nu(x)| on each link. The inequality telescopes over all finite chains. At isolated sites the pointwise costs vanish between any two isolated sites, giving an exact zero-cost coupling once active coordinates match. Conservation proves the iff threshold and norm coercivity. Definitions were checked against arXiv:2611.15938v1 Theorem 3.4 and Appendix A; 275 LP checks and the rational counterexample reproduced.

originality.rationale: The precise infimal-chain pseudometric is posed without a separation criterion in arXiv:2611.15938v1, Appendix A. Its proved localized transport metric is a different, generally larger object and the inequality points in the wrong direction to imply this lower bound. Nearby kernel-localization papers provide upper stability only. Semantic indexed searches and web phrase searches did not show a covering result; residual unindexed-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: Equivalent unpublished or unindexed lower-bound derivations may exist.
